title: Cone Volume Practice Exam
description: Practice deriving and applying cone volume from a matching cylinder comparison.

questions.question: A cone and a cylinder have the same radius and height. If the cylinder's volume is $90\text{ cm}^3$, what is the cone's volume?
questions.explanation: A cone with the same base and height has one-third the volume of the cylinder. $90 \div 3 = 30$, so the cone volume is $30\text{ cm}^3$.

questions.question: A cone has radius 3 cm and height 6 cm. Use $\pi = 3.14$. What is its volume in cubic centimeters? Enter a number only.
Which formula finds the volume of a cone?
questions.explanation: A cylinder has volume $\pi r^2h$. A matching cone has one-third of that volume, so $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h$.

questions.question: If a cone's diameter is 12 m, then $r = 12$ should be used in the volume formula.
questions.explanation: The formula uses radius, not diameter. If the diameter is 12 m, then the radius is $12 \div 2 = 6$ m.

questions.question: A cone has diameter 8 in. and height 9 in. Use $\pi = 3.14$. What is the volume?
In one or two sentences, explain why cone volume is one-third of the matching cylinder volume.
questions.correctAnswer: A cone with the same circular base and height as a cylinder has one-third of the cylinder's volume. Three congruent cones fill the matching cylinder.
questions.explanation: The key idea is the matching base and height. The cylinder volume is $\pi r^2h$, and the cone is one-third of that amount.

questions.question: A cone has radius 5 ft and height 12 ft. Use $\pi = 3.14$. What is its volume in cubic feet? Enter a number only.
A cone-shaped cup has radius 2 cm and height 15 cm. Which unit should be used for its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume measures three-dimensional space, so the correct unit is cubic centimeters, written $\text{cm}^3$.
